key_insight: A non-resonant acoustic streaming force, combined with a static pressure gradient, can unpin trapped oil droplets in capillary tubes by overcoming capillary pinning thresholds.
engineering_relevance: The model provides a power-efficient design rule for downhole or pore-scale acoustic tools to mobilize trapped non-wetting phases in porous formations.
method: Derive a second-order hydrodynamic model for acoustic-wind force density from attenuated first-order waves.
Compute the critical acoustic amplitude needed to exceed capillary pinning.
Include wall boundary-layer and bulk thermo-viscous losses to obtain an optimal absorption condition and transport velocity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical validation of the optimum condition and cross-correlation with legacy industrial frequency baselines.
watch_item: The optimum and unpinning predictions depend on idealized capillary geometry and damping assumptions, so real formations may require calibration for pore heterogeneity and frequency-dependent attenuation.
paper_title: Unpinning of trapped oil droplets via non-resonant acoustic streaming in capillary tubes
